## Why it matters

- **The mirror image of accreted standards.** [[2026-09-26-pocock-coding-standards-accretion]] keeps an agent aligned going forward (log failures → rules); Ebers' ask points the agent *backward* at accumulated drift — "here's everything we shipped fast, tell me what the architecture now actually is." Both attack the same problem: humans losing the structural picture when velocity is high.
- **Same family as /retro.** [[2026-09-26-pocock-retro-pr-talk]] — a scheduled look back at merged PRs to extract what was learned. An architecture-review prompt is a heavier, on-demand retro at the repo scale. Candidate pattern for our own fastest-moving scaffolding: periodic agent-run architecture summaries that diff *intended* vs *actual* structure.
- **Skepticism gates:** the tweet truncates exactly at the payload — the prompt itself, what Claude was given (full repo? file list?), and any verdict/output are all in the un-viewed video; "crazy idea" framing suggests experiment, not evaluated practice; 62 replies = interest, not validation. Treat as a pointer to a pattern, not evidence it works.
